exit_facts.description: The authorised cause of an employer's termination (Labor Code arts. 298–299); the broad exit reason does not tell labour-saving devices from retrenchment, or a closure for serious losses from one without.

exit_facts.label: Terminated for disease (Labor Code art.299)
exit_facts.description: Whether the employer ended the employment because the employee suffers from a disease whose continued employment is prohibited by law or prejudicial to the employee's or co-employees' health (Labor Code art.299, formerly art.284; E-Library PD 442 text art.323). The employer must pay separation pay of at least one month's salary or half a month per year of service, whichever is greater, a fraction of at least six months counting as a year. Asked on every non-domestic dismissal or unilateral termination; a kasambahay's disease is a just cause without separation pay (RA 10361 s.34(f)). Added in place 2026-09-29 in every version (a transcription omission: the article predates every version).

change_summary: The base law: SSS 15% under RA 11199 with Circular 2024-006, SSS_EC ₱30, PhilHealth 5% between ₱10,000 and ₱100,000, HDMF 2%/2% on a ₱10,000 fund salary, the TRAIN withholding table, the Labor Code working-time rules and the statutory leave types. No later change of law moves a seeded value (RR 29-2025 and the wage orders touch unmodelled caps — see the lineage README). Correction R45, 26 September 2026: RR 11-2018 s.2.79(B)(3),(5)(a). Taxable regular compensation excludes variable overtime/night premiums and leave encashment; deduct mandatory contributions before testing the cumulative trigger; ordinary withholding retains the regular-pay bracket. Corrects the snapshot without changing statutory commencement dates, tax rates or exemption ceilings. R46: missing registration does not waive compulsory SSS, mandatory provident fund, EC, PhilHealth or HDMF contributions, nor BIR RR 11-2018 s.9 withholding by the applicable table; each scheme still applies its coverage and rate rules.

limits.authority: Labor Code of the Philippines art.83

RA 10361 s.20: "an aggregate daily rest period of eight (8) hours per day", so at most sixteen worked hours in a day; a break is rest (https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/51514). The weekly rest (s.21, 24 consecutive hours a week) is met by `weekly_rest`, a rest after six consecutive work days (Labor Code art.91), which leaves no calendar week without one.

work_rules.authority: Labor Code of the Philippines (P.D. 442, as amended) Book III: art.82 (coverage), art.83 (eight-hour day), art.85 (meal period), art.86 (night shift differential), art.87 (overtime), art.91 (weekly rest day), art.93 (rest-day premium) and art.94 (holiday pay), with Proclamation No. 1006, s.2025 for the 2026 regular holidays and special (non-working) days. Applied 2026-09-18 (2): art.86 and Handbook ch.5: the night shift differential is 10% of the hour’s own rate, so 13 on a rest day or a special day, 20 on a regular holiday, 26 on a regular holiday falling on the rest day, 15 on a special day on the rest day, and on the overtime hours of each 12.5, 16.9, 26, 33.8 and 19.5 (`night_premium` adds as expressions over the day; the first eight night hours of a rest day or holiday are its ordinary ones). Handbook ch.2 §D–E: a monthly-paid employee — one "paid every day of the month, including unworked rest days, special days, and regular holidays", declared on the contract as `terms.paid_rest_days` (applied 2026-09-23, round 4: the payroll group is the employer’s own label and states no law) — is prorated and has an absence deducted on the 365 factor, 30.4167 a month (`proration_by`); the daily-paid keep 21.75 or 26.0833. Applied 2026-09-19 (2): The night-differential ladder reads the day type (`day_type`, which the holiday takes under `holiday_rest_precedence: PUBLIC_HOLIDAY`); `holiday.kind` is the published row’s kind (PUBLIC | SPECIAL | SUBSTITUTE), and a day-type literal against it never matched. Applied 2026-09-23 (PH audit): Handbook ch.2 §D, ch.3 §C, ch.4 §D state each day's pay as a total — a regular holiday worked 200%, a special day 130%, a rest day 130%, a regular holiday on the rest day 260%, a special day on the rest day 150%. The salary (261, 313 and 365 factors alike) and the daily-paid roster already pay a working holiday at 100%, so its first eight hours add the rest: 100% and 30% (`OT-2.0X`, `OT-1.3X`). The 365 factor (`terms.paid_rest_days`) also pays the rest day in the salary, so on it the rest-day rows add 30%, 160% and 50%; every other employee's rest day is unpaid and the rows carry the whole 130%, 260% and 150%. Hours beyond eight are paid by no base and keep their whole 169%, 260%, 338% and 195%. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 2): DOLE Handbook (2022) ch.2 §C: where two regular holidays fall on one day (a `DOUBLE_HOLIDAY` calendar row), the day is at least 200% of the daily wage unworked (`DOUBLE-HOLIDAY-UNWORKED`: a second day’s wage) and 300% worked (`OT-3.0X`: two more days on top of the day the wage pays); the guide computations (ch.4 §D) give 390% on a rest day (`OT-3.9X-REST`, 290% for the 365-factor employee, `terms.paid_rest_days`, whose salary pays the rest day), overtime 3 × 1.3 = 390% (`OT-3.9X`) and 3.9 × 1.3 = 507% on a rest day (`OT-5.07X-REST`), and night shift 10% of those rates (30, 39; overtime 39, 50.7). Ch.2 §D–E: an unworked regular holiday is paid only to an employee present, or on leave with pay, on the workday immediately preceding it (a rest or non-work day looks back further; two successive holidays pass the test through the first); `payroll.regular_holiday_prior_workday` applies it to the daily-paid wage and `holiday.prior_day_present` to the double holiday’s second day.

wages.authority: Applied 2026-09-18 (2): the wage orders state a daily rate; `by_region` carries it × 313/12 and `wages.scale` restates the floor on the person’s own factor — 365/12 for the monthly-paid, 261/12 on a five-day week, 313/12 on a six-day one — and the apprentice’s 75% (RA 6727; Labor Code arts.61, 75). Applied 2026-09-19 (3): Wage Order No. IVA-22 (effective 5 Oct 2025; nwpc.dole.gov.ph/region-iva): non-agriculture ₱600 in the Extended Metropolitan Area and the component cities (`IV-A`), ₱550 in 1st-class municipalities, ₱510 in reclassified 1st-class and 2nd–5th-class municipalities, the last two stepping to ₱550 and ₱525 on 1 April 2026 — the version from that date carries the second tranche. Each figure is the daily rate × 313 ÷ 12. Applied 2026-09-23 (audit): sector floors beside the area ones, for an establishment whose `company.region` names its sector — `NCR-AGRI-SMALL` is NCR agriculture, service/retail of 15 workers or fewer and manufacturing under 10 (₱658 under NCR-26, ₱718 under NCR-28; nwpc.dole.gov.ph/ncr/); `IV-A-RETAIL-SMALL` is IV-A retail/service of 10 workers or fewer (₱485 under IVA-22 from 5 Oct 2025, ₱508 from 1 Apr 2026; nwpc.dole.gov.ph/region-iva/). Each × 313 ÷ 12. The RA 9504 minimum-wage-earner test reads the same floor, so an employee of such an establishment above the sector floor is withheld on. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 2): RA 10361 (Batas Kasambahay) s.24: a domestic worker’s floor is the regional board’s domestic-worker wage order, a monthly figure, never the establishment order — `by_employment_type.DOMESTIC`, held on its own (scale 1). NCR only, from the wage orders themselves: NCR-DW-05 ₱7,000 a month from 4 January 2025, and NCR-DW-06 (approved 15 January 2026, published 22 January, effective 7 February 2026; nwpc.dole.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Wage-Order-No.-NCR-DW-06.pdf) ₱7,800 — this version states ₱7,000. Other regions’ domestic orders are not transcribed. Applied 2026-09-28 (issue 19, PH-A3): the floor is mandatory — RA 6727 s.4 and Wage Order No. NCR-28 s.4 (the increase applies to “all minimum wage earners in the private sector within the region”) and s.6 (non-payment is dealt with under RA 6727 s.12); only an exemption the board approves on application (RA 6727 s.4(c)) lowers it, recorded as `company.facts.minimum_wage_exemption_approved` (default false: no approval, no exemption). A covered under-floor contract therefore refuses the run (`block_below_when`). Applied 2026-09-30 (PH-A3 re-verification): a part-timer is refused too. The order’s daily rate is for normal working hours of at most eight a day and covers every minimum wage earner regardless of status (NCR-28 ss.3–4), and a worker on less than the normal hours is owed a proportion of it (DOLE Handbook 2024 ch.1 §L), so `wages.scale` multiplies a PART_TIME contract’s floor by its weekly hours over the full-time week of the person’s own factor (40 on a five-day week, 48 on a six-day one): the reference week is a recorded default, the orders naming none (20 hours on a five-day NCR-26 week: 695 × 261 ÷ 12 × 20 ÷ 40 = 7,558.13). The message quotes the floor on the person's own factor (₱755 × 261 ÷ 12 = 16,421.25 on a five-day week), not the 313-day basis. Applied 2026-09-29 (signed NWPC board orders): additional private daily rates are II ₱500; domestic monthly rates are I ₱6,700, II ₱6,500, III ₱6,500, IV-A ₱6,750, V ₱6,000, VI ₱6,500, XII ₱6,000, VII ₱7,000. The order PDFs are in this version’s sources. The private-sector exemption approval fact cannot displace a domestic floor; the inspected orders that address exemption expressly disallow it. Unrepresented mid-interval cutovers, area/sector/headcount selection and worksite-region selection remain open. Signed uniform private-sector tranche rates added for complete sealed intervals only: V ₱435/day, XIII ₱435/day. Region V RBV-22 reaches ₱435 on 1 December 2025; Caraga RXIII-19 reaches ₱435 on 1 May 2025 and RXIII-20 sets ₱455 from 3 January 2026, ₱475 from 1 May 2026. Intervals containing a later tranche remain without that regional rate pending an exact sealed version boundary. Signed predecessor domestic orders also establish complete-interval monthly rates: IV-B ₱6,500, X ₱6,000, XIII ₱6,000. Their orders are listed in this version’s sources; no mid-interval successor is applied to this sealed interval.

encashment.day_amount: terms.pay_frequency == "WEEKLY" ? terms.basic_salary / (terms.paid_rest_days ? 7.0 : terms.working_days_per_week) : terms.pay_frequency == "DAILY" ? terms.basic_salary : terms.pay_frequency == "HOURLY" ? terms.basic_salary * terms.ordinary_hours_per_week / terms.working_days_per_week : terms.basic_salary / (terms.paid_rest_days ? 365.0 / 12.0 : (terms.working_days_per_week >= 6.0 ? 313.0 : 261.0) / 12.0)
encashment.authority: DOLE Handbook on Workers Statutory Monetary Benefits, Service Incentive Leave, Conversion: salary rate on the conversion date, with pro-rata conversion. A daily contract supplies its daily salary; an hourly contract uses its normal scheduled hours per workday. Monthly equivalent factors follow paid-day coverage. Standing allowances require express basic-salary classification. https://nwpc.dole.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/Workers-Statutory-Monetary-Benefits-Handbook-2024-Edition.pdf Applied 2026-09-23 (round 5): a weekly contract converts at the same salary rate on the conversion date — its week's wage over the days that wage pays: the working days of the week, or all seven where the contract pays the rest day too (the Handbook's monthly-paid/daily-paid distinction, Rules on EEMR factors 365 and 313/261, applied to a week).

benefit_cases.authority: RA 11210 ss.3 and 5 and its IRR: 105 days' maternity leave with full pay for a live birth, 60 for a miscarriage or emergency termination, 15 more for a qualified solo parent, at least 60 days after delivery; the SSS maternity benefit is the average daily salary credit (the six highest of the twelve monthly salary credits, capped at PHP 20,000, before the semester of contingency, divided by 180) times the compensable days, with at least three monthly contributions paid in that twelve-month window, for a contingency on or after 11 March 2019; the employer advances it within 30 days of the application and SSS reimburses it. DOLE Department Advisory 01-2019 ss.II–IV: the salary differential is full pay (monthly salary × days ÷ 30) less the employee's SSS, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG shares and the SSS benefit, never negative; the exemption categories need DOLE approval. BIR RMC 105-2019: both are exempt from withholding. RA 11861 ss.15 and 20: the solo-parent identification card or eligibility certificate, first-time applicants within six months of the event.

sources.instructions:
Sources are the primary instrument first — the statute or regulation in the national law database, the gazette, or the table the authority itself publishes — one page per fact the version seals, never a news article or a commentary. A historical version lists the instruments in force on its own effective date. Where the primary host refuses the reader (sso.agc.gov.sg, officialgazette.gov.ph, peraturan.bpk.go.id, kwsp.gov.my, hrdcorp.gov.my answer 403 to Norbital-Public-Page-Reader) the authority’s own published table is listed instead, or the Wayback Machine’s dated copy of the authority’s own page or PDF (web.archive.org/web/<timestamp>id_/<url>) — never a host the reader cannot open.
officialgazette.gov.ph — the Official Gazette: Republic Acts, proclamations, executive orders. A proclamation is /<yyyy>/<mm>/<dd>/proclamation-no-<n>-s-<year>/ (HTML, full text); /section/proclamations/ lists the newest first; /nationwide-holidays/<year>/ is the holiday calendar. lawphil.net mirrors the same texts and is corroboration only.
sss.gov.ph — /pay-contribution/ carries the contribution schedule (the 2025 table PDF under /wp-content/uploads/ is 6.3 MB, over the reader limit: read the HTML page); /sss-circulars/ lists circulars by year.
philhealth.gov.ph — /advisories/<year>/ lists advisories; each is /advisories/<year>/PA<year>-<nnnn>.pdf (small, text). the premium schedule is PhilHealth Circular 2020-0005 (Revision 1), /circulars/2020/circ2020-0005.pdf (5 scanned pages, no text layer: §V.A the table, §V.B the equal employee/employer split), which each CY advisory cites; /partners/employers/ContributionTable_v2.pdf is the superseded 2019-0009 infographic and is not an authority.
pagibigfund.gov.ph serves a reCAPTCHA page, not the PDF: cite Circular 460 (15 January 2024, from February 2024; the 1%/2% tiers and the ₱10,000 fund salary cap) from its copy annexed to DMW Advisory 37-2025 (https://wcms.dmw.gov.ph/uploads/DMW_ADVISORY_37_2025_01225b9fec.pdf, 6 scanned pages, Circular 460 on pp.2–6), and Circular 275 from the Wayback copy (https://web.archive.org/web/2020id_/https://www.pagibigfund.gov.ph/document/pdf/circulars/provident/HDMF%20Circular%20275%20-%20Implementing%20Guidelines%20on%20Employer%20Registration%20Contribution%20and%20Remittance.pdf).
bir.gov.ph — bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/local/pdf/Annex E RR 11-2018.pdf is the withholding table (monthly and semi-monthly columns, 0.3 MB); revenue regulation digests are under bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/.
nwpc.dole.gov.ph — regional wage orders: /ncr/, /region-iva/ (and the other regions); /bwc-handbook-workers-statutory-monetary-benefits/ is the DOLE Handbook (factors, premiums, 13th month).
pco.gov.ph answers 403 to the reader; use the Gazette.

Finding changes (read these before comparing, every run):
Wage orders: read https://nwpc.dole.gov.ph/feed/ (RSS) for new RTWPB orders, then open https://nwpc.dole.gov.ph/statistics/summary-of-latest-wage-orders-issued-by-the-regional-boards/ and follow its 'Download PDF' (Latest-Wage-Order-Matrix-<date>.pdf, a text PDF with issue/publication/effectivity per region). Effectivity is 15 days after publication when the matrix leaves it blank. The regional pages (/ncr/, /region-iva/ …) link the signed wage-order PDFs. These are scans with no text layer, so take the figures from the matrix. SSS: newest CI number on /sss-circulars/, and the rate table on /pay-contribution/. PhilHealth: /advisories/<YYYY>/ and /circulars/<YYYY>/; premium changes are 'Premium Contribution … for CY<YYYY>' advisories. BIR: every www.bir.gov.ph listing (RR, RMC, WithHoldingTax) is a client-rendered shell ('Loading…'), so it cannot be read. Discover RR/RMC numbers from a big-4 alert list (PwC PH Tax Alerts, SGV/EY Tax Bulletin), then open the PDF at https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/RR%20No.%20<n>-<yyyy>.pdf. Holidays: lawphil proclamation index for discovery only (officialgazette.gov.ph returns 403). Pag-IBIG and DOLE/BWC labor advisories are bot-walled: use news only to discover, and do not cite them.

facts.label: Regularly fewer than ten employees
facts.description: Whether the establishment regularly employs fewer than ten employees: outside service incentive leave (Labor Code art.95(b); Omnibus Rules Book III Rule V s.1(e); DOLE Handbook on Workers’ Statutory Monetary Benefits 2023, SIL B.8). A count of the establishment, with no statutory default: required.

facts.label: Retail, service or agricultural establishment of ten or fewer
facts.description: Whether the establishment is a retail, service or agricultural establishment or operation employing not more than ten employees: outside RA 7641 retirement pay (Labor Code art.302). A different test from `small_establishment` (any sector, fewer than ten), with no statutory default: required.

facts.label: Exempted from the wage order by the regional board
facts.description: Whether the regional wages board has approved this establishment's application for exemption from the wage order in force (RA 6727 s.4(c); DOLE Administrative Order No. 264, series of 2026, on exemptions). Without it a covered contract below the floor refuses the run. Default false: an exemption exists only once approved.

exit_facts.label: Labor Code authorised cause
exit_facts.description: The authorised cause of an employer's termination (Labor Code arts. 298–299); the broad exit reason does not tell labour-saving devices from retrenchment, or a closure for serious losses from one without.

exit_facts.label: Terminated for disease (Labor Code art.299)
exit_facts.description: Whether the employer ended the employment because the employee suffers from a disease whose continued employment is prohibited by law or prejudicial to the employee's or co-employees' health (Labor Code art.299, formerly art.284; E-Library PD 442 text art.323). The employer must pay separation pay of at least one month's salary or half a month per year of service, whichever is greater, a fraction of at least six months counting as a year. Asked on every non-domestic dismissal or unilateral termination; a kasambahay's disease is a just cause without separation pay (RA 10361 s.34(f)). Added in place 2026-09-29 in every version (a transcription omission: the article predates every version).

exit_facts.label: Kasambahay dismissed without just cause
exit_facts.description: Whether a domestic worker was dismissed without a cause RA 10361 s.34 lists: an unjust dismissal pays the compensation earned plus fifteen days’ work as indemnity (s.32).

exit_facts.label: Kasambahay left without justifiable reason
exit_facts.description: RA 10361 s.32: unpaid salary of up to fifteen days is forfeited when the worker leaves without justifiable reason.

name: Philippines — withholding correction R45 (R46 withholding registration)
void_reason: Superseded by 42192a1f-4f4a-5172-ab20-38904eae68d7 to refuse SSS/MPF assessment when compulsory-coverage age is unknown; original catalogues retained.
change_summary: No change of law. This version exists to carry the STATUTORY_ADJUSTMENT payment code the company records name from January 2026; every statutory row is a clone of the 2025-12-01 version. The next change of law (a 2027 wage order, an SSS or PhilHealth circular) is a new version from its own date. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 3): RR 29-2025 commences on 6 January 2026, not 1 January, so this version keeps RR 11-2018’s de minimis rice ceiling (₱2,000) and 10-day leave cash-out; the version of 6 January 2026 carries the new figures. Correction R45, 26 September 2026: RR 11-2018 s.2.79(B)(3),(5)(a). Taxable regular compensation excludes variable overtime/night premiums and leave encashment; deduct mandatory contributions before testing the cumulative trigger; ordinary withholding retains the regular-pay bracket. Corrects the snapshot without changing statutory commencement dates, tax rates or exemption ceilings. R46: missing registration does not waive compulsory SSS, mandatory provident fund, EC, PhilHealth or HDMF contributions, nor BIR RR 11-2018 s.9 withholding by the applicable table; each scheme still applies its coverage and rate rules.

limits.authority: Labor Code of the Philippines art.83

RA 10361 s.20: "an aggregate daily rest period of eight (8) hours per day", so at most sixteen worked hours in a day; a break is rest (https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/51514). The weekly rest (s.21, 24 consecutive hours a week) is met by `weekly_rest`, a rest after six consecutive work days (Labor Code art.91), which leaves no calendar week without one.

work_rules.authority: Labor Code of the Philippines (P.D. 442, as amended) Book III: art.82 (coverage), art.83 (eight-hour day), art.85 (meal period), art.86 (night shift differential), art.87 (overtime), art.91 (weekly rest day), art.93 (rest-day premium) and art.94 (holiday pay), with Proclamation No. 1006, s.2025 for the 2026 regular holidays and special (non-working) days. Applied 2026-09-18 (2): art.86 and Handbook ch.5: the night shift differential is 10% of the hour’s own rate, so 13 on a rest day or a special day, 20 on a regular holiday, 26 on a regular holiday falling on the rest day, 15 on a special day on the rest day, and on the overtime hours of each 12.5, 16.9, 26, 33.8 and 19.5 (`night_premium` adds as expressions over the day; the first eight night hours of a rest day or holiday are its ordinary ones). Handbook ch.2 §D–E: a monthly-paid employee — one "paid every day of the month, including unworked rest days, special days, and regular holidays", declared on the contract as `terms.paid_rest_days` (applied 2026-09-23, round 4: the payroll group is the employer’s own label and states no law) — is prorated and has an absence deducted on the 365 factor, 30.4167 a month (`proration_by`); the daily-paid keep 21.75 or 26.0833. Applied 2026-09-19 (2): The night-differential ladder reads the day type (`day_type`, which the holiday takes under `holiday_rest_precedence: PUBLIC_HOLIDAY`); `holiday.kind` is the published row’s kind (PUBLIC | SPECIAL | SUBSTITUTE), and a day-type literal against it never matched. Applied 2026-09-23 (PH audit): Handbook ch.2 §D, ch.3 §C, ch.4 §D state each day's pay as a total — a regular holiday worked 200%, a special day 130%, a rest day 130%, a regular holiday on the rest day 260%, a special day on the rest day 150%. The salary (261, 313 and 365 factors alike) and the daily-paid roster already pay a working holiday at 100%, so its first eight hours add the rest: 100% and 30% (`OT-2.0X`, `OT-1.3X`). The 365 factor (`terms.paid_rest_days`) also pays the rest day in the salary, so on it the rest-day rows add 30%, 160% and 50%; every other employee's rest day is unpaid and the rows carry the whole 130%, 260% and 150%. Hours beyond eight are paid by no base and keep their whole 169%, 260%, 338% and 195%. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 2): DOLE Handbook (2022) ch.2 §C: where two regular holidays fall on one day (a `DOUBLE_HOLIDAY` calendar row), the day is at least 200% of the daily wage unworked (`DOUBLE-HOLIDAY-UNWORKED`: a second day’s wage) and 300% worked (`OT-3.0X`: two more days on top of the day the wage pays); the guide computations (ch.4 §D) give 390% on a rest day (`OT-3.9X-REST`, 290% for the 365-factor employee, `terms.paid_rest_days`, whose salary pays the rest day), overtime 3 × 1.3 = 390% (`OT-3.9X`) and 3.9 × 1.3 = 507% on a rest day (`OT-5.07X-REST`), and night shift 10% of those rates (30, 39; overtime 39, 50.7). Ch.2 §D–E: an unworked regular holiday is paid only to an employee present, or on leave with pay, on the workday immediately preceding it (a rest or non-work day looks back further; two successive holidays pass the test through the first); `payroll.regular_holiday_prior_workday` applies it to the daily-paid wage and `holiday.prior_day_present` to the double holiday’s second day.

wages.authority: Applied 2026-09-18 (2): the wage orders state a daily rate; `by_region` carries it × 313/12 and `wages.scale` restates the floor on the person’s own factor — 365/12 for the monthly-paid, 261/12 on a five-day week, 313/12 on a six-day one — and the apprentice’s 75% (RA 6727; Labor Code arts.61, 75). Applied 2026-09-19 (3): Wage Order No. IVA-22 (effective 5 Oct 2025; nwpc.dole.gov.ph/region-iva): non-agriculture ₱600 in the Extended Metropolitan Area and the component cities (`IV-A`), ₱550 in 1st-class municipalities, ₱510 in reclassified 1st-class and 2nd–5th-class municipalities, the last two stepping to ₱550 and ₱525 on 1 April 2026 — the version from that date carries the second tranche. Each figure is the daily rate × 313 ÷ 12. Applied 2026-09-23 (audit): sector floors beside the area ones, for an establishment whose `company.region` names its sector — `NCR-AGRI-SMALL` is NCR agriculture, service/retail of 15 workers or fewer and manufacturing under 10 (₱658 under NCR-26, ₱718 under NCR-28; nwpc.dole.gov.ph/ncr/); `IV-A-RETAIL-SMALL` is IV-A retail/service of 10 workers or fewer (₱485 under IVA-22 from 5 Oct 2025, ₱508 from 1 Apr 2026; nwpc.dole.gov.ph/region-iva/). Each × 313 ÷ 12. The RA 9504 minimum-wage-earner test reads the same floor, so an employee of such an establishment above the sector floor is withheld on. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 2): RA 10361 (Batas Kasambahay) s.24: a domestic worker’s floor is the regional board’s domestic-worker wage order, a monthly figure, never the establishment order — `by_employment_type.DOMESTIC`, held on its own (scale 1). NCR only, from the wage orders themselves: NCR-DW-05 ₱7,000 a month from 4 January 2025, and NCR-DW-06 (approved 15 January 2026, published 22 January, effective 7 February 2026; nwpc.dole.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Wage-Order-No.-NCR-DW-06.pdf) ₱7,800 — from the version of 7 February 2026; this version, which closes before it, states ₱7,000. Other regions’ domestic orders are not transcribed. Applied 2026-09-28 (issue 19, PH-A3): the floor is mandatory — RA 6727 s.4 and Wage Order No. NCR-28 s.4 (the increase applies to “all minimum wage earners in the private sector within the region”) and s.6 (non-payment is dealt with under RA 6727 s.12); only an exemption the board approves on application (RA 6727 s.4(c)) lowers it, recorded as `company.facts.minimum_wage_exemption_approved` (default false: no approval, no exemption). A covered under-floor contract therefore refuses the run (`block_below_when`). Applied 2026-09-30 (PH-A3 re-verification): a part-timer is refused too. The order’s daily rate is for normal working hours of at most eight a day and covers every minimum wage earner regardless of status (NCR-28 ss.3–4), and a worker on less than the normal hours is owed a proportion of it (DOLE Handbook 2024 ch.1 §L), so `wages.scale` multiplies a PART_TIME contract’s floor by its weekly hours over the full-time week of the person’s own factor (40 on a five-day week, 48 on a six-day one): the reference week is a recorded default, the orders naming none (20 hours on a five-day NCR-26 week: 695 × 261 ÷ 12 × 20 ÷ 40 = 7,558.13). The message quotes the floor on the person's own factor (₱755 × 261 ÷ 12 = 16,421.25 on a five-day week), not the 313-day basis. Applied 2026-09-29 (signed NWPC board orders): additional private daily rates are II ₱500, CAR ₱505, IV-B ₱455; domestic monthly rates are I ₱6,700, II ₱6,500, III ₱6,500, IV-A ₱6,750, V ₱6,000, VI ₱6,500, XII ₱6,000, VII ₱7,000, CAR ₱6,600, IV-B ₱7,000. The order PDFs are in this version’s sources. The private-sector exemption approval fact cannot displace a domestic floor; the inspected orders that address exemption expressly disallow it. Unrepresented mid-interval cutovers, area/sector/headcount selection and worksite-region selection remain open. Signed uniform private-sector tranche rates added for complete sealed intervals only: V ₱435/day. Region V RBV-22 reaches ₱435 on 1 December 2025; Caraga RXIII-19 reaches ₱435 on 1 May 2025 and RXIII-20 sets ₱455 from 3 January 2026, ₱475 from 1 May 2026. Intervals containing a later tranche remain without that regional rate pending an exact sealed version boundary. Signed predecessor domestic orders also establish complete-interval monthly rates: X ₱6,000. Their orders are listed in this version’s sources; no mid-interval successor is applied to this sealed interval.

encashment.day_amount: terms.pay_frequency == "WEEKLY" ? terms.basic_salary / (terms.paid_rest_days ? 7.0 : terms.working_days_per_week) : terms.pay_frequency == "DAILY" ? terms.basic_salary : terms.pay_frequency == "HOURLY" ? terms.basic_salary * terms.ordinary_hours_per_week / terms.working_days_per_week : terms.basic_salary / (terms.paid_rest_days ? 365.0 / 12.0 : (terms.working_days_per_week >= 6.0 ? 313.0 : 261.0) / 12.0)
encashment.authority: DOLE Handbook on Workers Statutory Monetary Benefits, Service Incentive Leave, Conversion: salary rate on the conversion date, with pro-rata conversion. A daily contract supplies its daily salary; an hourly contract uses its normal scheduled hours per workday. Monthly equivalent factors follow paid-day coverage. Standing allowances require express basic-salary classification. https://nwpc.dole.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/Workers-Statutory-Monetary-Benefits-Handbook-2024-Edition.pdf Applied 2026-09-23 (round 5): a weekly contract converts at the same salary rate on the conversion date — its week's wage over the days that wage pays: the working days of the week, or all seven where the contract pays the rest day too (the Handbook's monthly-paid/daily-paid distinction, Rules on EEMR factors 365 and 313/261, applied to a week).

benefit_cases.authority: RA 11210 ss.3 and 5 and its IRR: 105 days' maternity leave with full pay for a live birth, 60 for a miscarriage or emergency termination, 15 more for a qualified solo parent, at least 60 days after delivery; the SSS maternity benefit is the average daily salary credit (the six highest of the twelve monthly salary credits, capped at PHP 20,000, before the semester of contingency, divided by 180) times the compensable days, with at least three monthly contributions paid in that twelve-month window, for a contingency on or after 11 March 2019; the employer advances it within 30 days of the application and SSS reimburses it. DOLE Department Advisory 01-2019 ss.II–IV: the salary differential is full pay (monthly salary × days ÷ 30) less the employee's SSS, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG shares and the SSS benefit, never negative; the exemption categories need DOLE approval. BIR RMC 105-2019: both are exempt from withholding. RA 11861 ss.15 and 20: the solo-parent identification card or eligibility certificate, first-time applicants within six months of the event.

sources.instructions:
Sources are the primary instrument first — the statute or regulation in the national law database, the gazette, or the table the authority itself publishes — one page per fact the version seals, never a news article or a commentary. A historical version lists the instruments in force on its own effective date. Where the primary host refuses the reader (sso.agc.gov.sg, officialgazette.gov.ph, peraturan.bpk.go.id, kwsp.gov.my, hrdcorp.gov.my answer 403 to Norbital-Public-Page-Reader) the authority’s own published table is listed instead, or the Wayback Machine’s dated copy of the authority’s own page or PDF (web.archive.org/web/<timestamp>id_/<url>) — never a host the reader cannot open.
officialgazette.gov.ph — the Official Gazette: Republic Acts, proclamations, executive orders. A proclamation is /<yyyy>/<mm>/<dd>/proclamation-no-<n>-s-<year>/ (HTML, full text); /section/proclamations/ lists the newest first; /nationwide-holidays/<year>/ is the holiday calendar. lawphil.net mirrors the same texts and is corroboration only.
sss.gov.ph — /pay-contribution/ carries the contribution schedule (the 2025 table PDF under /wp-content/uploads/ is 6.3 MB, over the reader limit: read the HTML page); /sss-circulars/ lists circulars by year.
philhealth.gov.ph — /advisories/<year>/ lists advisories; each is /advisories/<year>/PA<year>-<nnnn>.pdf (small, text). the premium schedule is PhilHealth Circular 2020-0005 (Revision 1), /circulars/2020/circ2020-0005.pdf (5 scanned pages, no text layer: §V.A the table, §V.B the equal employee/employer split), which each CY advisory cites; /partners/employers/ContributionTable_v2.pdf is the superseded 2019-0009 infographic and is not an authority.
pagibigfund.gov.ph serves a reCAPTCHA page, not the PDF: cite Circular 460 (15 January 2024, from February 2024; the 1%/2% tiers and the ₱10,000 fund salary cap) from its copy annexed to DMW Advisory 37-2025 (https://wcms.dmw.gov.ph/uploads/DMW_ADVISORY_37_2025_01225b9fec.pdf, 6 scanned pages, Circular 460 on pp.2–6), and Circular 275 from the Wayback copy (https://web.archive.org/web/2020id_/https://www.pagibigfund.gov.ph/document/pdf/circulars/provident/HDMF%20Circular%20275%20-%20Implementing%20Guidelines%20on%20Employer%20Registration%20Contribution%20and%20Remittance.pdf).
bir.gov.ph — bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/local/pdf/Annex E RR 11-2018.pdf is the withholding table (monthly and semi-monthly columns, 0.3 MB); revenue regulation digests are under bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/.
nwpc.dole.gov.ph — regional wage orders: /ncr/, /region-iva/ (and the other regions); /bwc-handbook-workers-statutory-monetary-benefits/ is the DOLE Handbook (factors, premiums, 13th month).
pco.gov.ph answers 403 to the reader; use the Gazette.

Finding changes (read these before comparing, every run):
Wage orders: read https://nwpc.dole.gov.ph/feed/ (RSS) for new RTWPB orders, then open https://nwpc.dole.gov.ph/statistics/summary-of-latest-wage-orders-issued-by-the-regional-boards/ and follow its 'Download PDF' (Latest-Wage-Order-Matrix-<date>.pdf, a text PDF with issue/publication/effectivity per region). Effectivity is 15 days after publication when the matrix leaves it blank. The regional pages (/ncr/, /region-iva/ …) link the signed wage-order PDFs. These are scans with no text layer, so take the figures from the matrix. SSS: newest CI number on /sss-circulars/, and the rate table on /pay-contribution/. PhilHealth: /advisories/<YYYY>/ and /circulars/<YYYY>/; premium changes are 'Premium Contribution … for CY<YYYY>' advisories. BIR: every www.bir.gov.ph listing (RR, RMC, WithHoldingTax) is a client-rendered shell ('Loading…'), so it cannot be read. Discover RR/RMC numbers from a big-4 alert list (PwC PH Tax Alerts, SGV/EY Tax Bulletin), then open the PDF at https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/RR%20No.%20<n>-<yyyy>.pdf. Holidays: lawphil proclamation index for discovery only (officialgazette.gov.ph returns 403). Pag-IBIG and DOLE/BWC labor advisories are bot-walled: use news only to discover, and do not cite them.

facts.label: Regularly fewer than ten employees
facts.description: Whether the establishment regularly employs fewer than ten employees: outside service incentive leave (Labor Code art.95(b); Omnibus Rules Book III Rule V s.1(e); DOLE Handbook on Workers’ Statutory Monetary Benefits 2023, SIL B.8). A count of the establishment, with no statutory default: required.

facts.label: Retail, service or agricultural establishment of ten or fewer
facts.description: Whether the establishment is a retail, service or agricultural establishment or operation employing not more than ten employees: outside RA 7641 retirement pay (Labor Code art.302). A different test from `small_establishment` (any sector, fewer than ten), with no statutory default: required.

facts.label: Exempted from the wage order by the regional board
facts.description: Whether the regional wages board has approved this establishment's application for exemption from the wage order in force (RA 6727 s.4(c); DOLE Administrative Order No. 264, series of 2026, on exemptions). Without it a covered contract below the floor refuses the run. Default false: an exemption exists only once approved.

exit_facts.label: Labor Code authorised cause
exit_facts.description: The authorised cause of an employer's termination (Labor Code arts. 298–299); the broad exit reason does not tell labour-saving devices from retrenchment, or a closure for serious losses from one without.

exit_facts.label: Terminated for disease (Labor Code art.299)
exit_facts.description: Whether the employer ended the employment because the employee suffers from a disease whose continued employment is prohibited by law or prejudicial to the employee's or co-employees' health (Labor Code art.299, formerly art.284; E-Library PD 442 text art.323). The employer must pay separation pay of at least one month's salary or half a month per year of service, whichever is greater, a fraction of at least six months counting as a year. Asked on every non-domestic dismissal or unilateral termination; a kasambahay's disease is a just cause without separation pay (RA 10361 s.34(f)). Added in place 2026-09-29 in every version (a transcription omission: the article predates every version).

exit_facts.label: Kasambahay dismissed without just cause
exit_facts.description: Whether a domestic worker was dismissed without a cause RA 10361 s.34 lists: an unjust dismissal pays the compensation earned plus fifteen days’ work as indemnity (s.32).

exit_facts.label: Kasambahay left without justifiable reason
exit_facts.description: RA 10361 s.32: unpaid salary of up to fifteen days is forfeited when the worker leaves without justifiable reason.

name: Philippines — 6 January 2026 — withholding correction R45 (R46 withholding registration)
void_reason: Superseded by eb8a11b1-8914-5940-b3ab-37ba62f66fbf to refuse SSS/MPF assessment when compulsory-coverage age is unknown; original catalogues retained.
change_summary: RR 29-2025 (dated 27 October 2025, posted on the BIR website 22 December 2025, in force fifteen days later, 6 January 2026; s.3): de minimis rice subsidy ₱2,000 → ₱2,500 a month and monetised unused vacation leave 10 → 12 days a year in the WTAX base. Nothing else moves. Correction R45, 26 September 2026: RR 11-2018 s.2.79(B)(3),(5)(a). Taxable regular compensation excludes variable overtime/night premiums and leave encashment; deduct mandatory contributions before testing the cumulative trigger; ordinary withholding retains the regular-pay bracket. Corrects the snapshot without changing statutory commencement dates, tax rates or exemption ceilings. R46: missing registration does not waive compulsory SSS, mandatory provident fund, EC, PhilHealth or HDMF contributions, nor BIR RR 11-2018 s.9 withholding by the applicable table; each scheme still applies its coverage and rate rules.

limits.authority: Labor Code of the Philippines art.83

RA 10361 s.20: "an aggregate daily rest period of eight (8) hours per day", so at most sixteen worked hours in a day; a break is rest (https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/51514). The weekly rest (s.21, 24 consecutive hours a week) is met by `weekly_rest`, a rest after six consecutive work days (Labor Code art.91), which leaves no calendar week without one.

work_rules.authority: Labor Code of the Philippines (P.D. 442, as amended) Book III: art.82 (coverage), art.83 (eight-hour day), art.85 (meal period), art.86 (night shift differential), art.87 (overtime), art.91 (weekly rest day), art.93 (rest-day premium) and art.94 (holiday pay), with Proclamation No. 1006, s.2025 for the 2026 regular holidays and special (non-working) days. Applied 2026-09-18 (2): art.86 and Handbook ch.5: the night shift differential is 10% of the hour’s own rate, so 13 on a rest day or a special day, 20 on a regular holiday, 26 on a regular holiday falling on the rest day, 15 on a special day on the rest day, and on the overtime hours of each 12.5, 16.9, 26, 33.8 and 19.5 (`night_premium` adds as expressions over the day; the first eight night hours of a rest day or holiday are its ordinary ones). Handbook ch.2 §D–E: a monthly-paid employee — one "paid every day of the month, including unworked rest days, special days, and regular holidays", declared on the contract as `terms.paid_rest_days` (applied 2026-09-23, round 4: the payroll group is the employer’s own label and states no law) — is prorated and has an absence deducted on the 365 factor, 30.4167 a month (`proration_by`); the daily-paid keep 21.75 or 26.0833. Applied 2026-09-19 (2): The night-differential ladder reads the day type (`day_type`, which the holiday takes under `holiday_rest_precedence: PUBLIC_HOLIDAY`); `holiday.kind` is the published row’s kind (PUBLIC | SPECIAL | SUBSTITUTE), and a day-type literal against it never matched. Applied 2026-09-23 (PH audit): Handbook ch.2 §D, ch.3 §C, ch.4 §D state each day's pay as a total — a regular holiday worked 200%, a special day 130%, a rest day 130%, a regular holiday on the rest day 260%, a special day on the rest day 150%. The salary (261, 313 and 365 factors alike) and the daily-paid roster already pay a working holiday at 100%, so its first eight hours add the rest: 100% and 30% (`OT-2.0X`, `OT-1.3X`). The 365 factor (`terms.paid_rest_days`) also pays the rest day in the salary, so on it the rest-day rows add 30%, 160% and 50%; every other employee's rest day is unpaid and the rows carry the whole 130%, 260% and 150%. Hours beyond eight are paid by no base and keep their whole 169%, 260%, 338% and 195%. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 2): DOLE Handbook (2022) ch.2 §C: where two regular holidays fall on one day (a `DOUBLE_HOLIDAY` calendar row), the day is at least 200% of the daily wage unworked (`DOUBLE-HOLIDAY-UNWORKED`: a second day’s wage) and 300% worked (`OT-3.0X`: two more days on top of the day the wage pays); the guide computations (ch.4 §D) give 390% on a rest day (`OT-3.9X-REST`, 290% for the 365-factor employee, `terms.paid_rest_days`, whose salary pays the rest day), overtime 3 × 1.3 = 390% (`OT-3.9X`) and 3.9 × 1.3 = 507% on a rest day (`OT-5.07X-REST`), and night shift 10% of those rates (30, 39; overtime 39, 50.7). Ch.2 §D–E: an unworked regular holiday is paid only to an employee present, or on leave with pay, on the workday immediately preceding it (a rest or non-work day looks back further; two successive holidays pass the test through the first); `payroll.regular_holiday_prior_workday` applies it to the daily-paid wage and `holiday.prior_day_present` to the double holiday’s second day.

wages.authority: Applied 2026-09-18 (2): the wage orders state a daily rate; `by_region` carries it × 313/12 and `wages.scale` restates the floor on the person’s own factor — 365/12 for the monthly-paid, 261/12 on a five-day week, 313/12 on a six-day one — and the apprentice’s 75% (RA 6727; Labor Code arts.61, 75). Applied 2026-09-19 (3): Wage Order No. IVA-22 (effective 5 Oct 2025; nwpc.dole.gov.ph/region-iva): non-agriculture ₱600 in the Extended Metropolitan Area and the component cities (`IV-A`), ₱550 in 1st-class municipalities, ₱510 in reclassified 1st-class and 2nd–5th-class municipalities, the last two stepping to ₱550 and ₱525 on 1 April 2026 — the version from that date carries the second tranche. Each figure is the daily rate × 313 ÷ 12. Applied 2026-09-23 (audit): sector floors beside the area ones, for an establishment whose `company.region` names its sector — `NCR-AGRI-SMALL` is NCR agriculture, service/retail of 15 workers or fewer and manufacturing under 10 (₱658 under NCR-26, ₱718 under NCR-28; nwpc.dole.gov.ph/ncr/); `IV-A-RETAIL-SMALL` is IV-A retail/service of 10 workers or fewer (₱485 under IVA-22 from 5 Oct 2025, ₱508 from 1 Apr 2026; nwpc.dole.gov.ph/region-iva/). Each × 313 ÷ 12. The RA 9504 minimum-wage-earner test reads the same floor, so an employee of such an establishment above the sector floor is withheld on. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 2): RA 10361 (Batas Kasambahay) s.24: a domestic worker’s floor is the regional board’s domestic-worker wage order, a monthly figure, never the establishment order — `by_employment_type.DOMESTIC`, held on its own (scale 1). NCR only, from the wage orders themselves: NCR-DW-05 ₱7,000 a month from 4 January 2025, and NCR-DW-06 (approved 15 January 2026, published 22 January, effective 7 February 2026; nwpc.dole.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Wage-Order-No.-NCR-DW-06.pdf) ₱7,800 — from the version of 7 February 2026; this version, which closes before it, states ₱7,000. Other regions’ domestic orders are not transcribed. Applied 2026-09-28 (issue 19, PH-A3): the floor is mandatory — RA 6727 s.4 and Wage Order No. NCR-28 s.4 (the increase applies to “all minimum wage earners in the private sector within the region”) and s.6 (non-payment is dealt with under RA 6727 s.12); only an exemption the board approves on application (RA 6727 s.4(c)) lowers it, recorded as `company.facts.minimum_wage_exemption_approved` (default false: no approval, no exemption). A covered under-floor contract therefore refuses the run (`block_below_when`). Applied 2026-09-30 (PH-A3 re-verification): a part-timer is refused too. The order’s daily rate is for normal working hours of at most eight a day and covers every minimum wage earner regardless of status (NCR-28 ss.3–4), and a worker on less than the normal hours is owed a proportion of it (DOLE Handbook 2024 ch.1 §L), so `wages.scale` multiplies a PART_TIME contract’s floor by its weekly hours over the full-time week of the person’s own factor (40 on a five-day week, 48 on a six-day one): the reference week is a recorded default, the orders naming none (20 hours on a five-day NCR-26 week: 695 × 261 ÷ 12 × 20 ÷ 40 = 7,558.13). The message quotes the floor on the person's own factor (₱755 × 261 ÷ 12 = 16,421.25 on a five-day week), not the 313-day basis. Applied 2026-09-29 (signed NWPC board orders): additional private daily rates are II ₱500, CAR ₱505, IV-B ₱455; domestic monthly rates are I ₱6,700, II ₱6,500, III ₱6,500, IV-A ₱6,750, V ₱6,000, VI ₱6,500, XII ₱6,000, VII ₱7,000, CAR ₱6,600, IV-B ₱7,000, XIII ₱6,500. The order PDFs are in this version’s sources. The private-sector exemption approval fact cannot displace a domestic floor; the inspected orders that address exemption expressly disallow it. Unrepresented mid-interval cutovers, area/sector/headcount selection and worksite-region selection remain open. Signed uniform private-sector tranche rates added for complete sealed intervals only: V ₱435/day, XIII ₱455/day. Region V RBV-22 reaches ₱435 on 1 December 2025; Caraga RXIII-19 reaches ₱435 on 1 May 2025 and RXIII-20 sets ₱455 from 3 January 2026, ₱475 from 1 May 2026. Intervals containing a later tranche remain without that regional rate pending an exact sealed version boundary.

encashment.day_amount: terms.pay_frequency == "WEEKLY" ? terms.basic_salary / (terms.paid_rest_days ? 7.0 : terms.working_days_per_week) : terms.pay_frequency == "DAILY" ? terms.basic_salary : terms.pay_frequency == "HOURLY" ? terms.basic_salary * terms.ordinary_hours_per_week / terms.working_days_per_week : terms.basic_salary / (terms.paid_rest_days ? 365.0 / 12.0 : (terms.working_days_per_week >= 6.0 ? 313.0 : 261.0) / 12.0)
encashment.authority: DOLE Handbook on Workers Statutory Monetary Benefits, Service Incentive Leave, Conversion: salary rate on the conversion date, with pro-rata conversion. A daily contract supplies its daily salary; an hourly contract uses its normal scheduled hours per workday. Monthly equivalent factors follow paid-day coverage. Standing allowances require express basic-salary classification. https://nwpc.dole.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/Workers-Statutory-Monetary-Benefits-Handbook-2024-Edition.pdf Applied 2026-09-23 (round 5): a weekly contract converts at the same salary rate on the conversion date — its week's wage over the days that wage pays: the working days of the week, or all seven where the contract pays the rest day too (the Handbook's monthly-paid/daily-paid distinction, Rules on EEMR factors 365 and 313/261, applied to a week).

benefit_cases.authority: RA 11210 ss.3 and 5 and its IRR: 105 days' maternity leave with full pay for a live birth, 60 for a miscarriage or emergency termination, 15 more for a qualified solo parent, at least 60 days after delivery; the SSS maternity benefit is the average daily salary credit (the six highest of the twelve monthly salary credits, capped at PHP 20,000, before the semester of contingency, divided by 180) times the compensable days, with at least three monthly contributions paid in that twelve-month window, for a contingency on or after 11 March 2019; the employer advances it within 30 days of the application and SSS reimburses it. DOLE Department Advisory 01-2019 ss.II–IV: the salary differential is full pay (monthly salary × days ÷ 30) less the employee's SSS, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG shares and the SSS benefit, never negative; the exemption categories need DOLE approval. BIR RMC 105-2019: both are exempt from withholding. RA 11861 ss.15 and 20: the solo-parent identification card or eligibility certificate, first-time applicants within six months of the event.

sources.instructions:
Sources are the primary instrument first — the statute or regulation in the national law database, the gazette, or the table the authority itself publishes — one page per fact the version seals, never a news article or a commentary. A historical version lists the instruments in force on its own effective date. Where the primary host refuses the reader (sso.agc.gov.sg, officialgazette.gov.ph, peraturan.bpk.go.id, kwsp.gov.my, hrdcorp.gov.my answer 403 to Norbital-Public-Page-Reader) the authority’s own published table is listed instead, or the Wayback Machine’s dated copy of the authority’s own page or PDF (web.archive.org/web/<timestamp>id_/<url>) — never a host the reader cannot open.
officialgazette.gov.ph — the Official Gazette: Republic Acts, proclamations, executive orders. A proclamation is /<yyyy>/<mm>/<dd>/proclamation-no-<n>-s-<year>/ (HTML, full text); /section/proclamations/ lists the newest first; /nationwide-holidays/<year>/ is the holiday calendar. lawphil.net mirrors the same texts and is corroboration only.
sss.gov.ph — /pay-contribution/ carries the contribution schedule (the 2025 table PDF under /wp-content/uploads/ is 6.3 MB, over the reader limit: read the HTML page); /sss-circulars/ lists circulars by year.
philhealth.gov.ph — /advisories/<year>/ lists advisories; each is /advisories/<year>/PA<year>-<nnnn>.pdf (small, text). the premium schedule is PhilHealth Circular 2020-0005 (Revision 1), /circulars/2020/circ2020-0005.pdf (5 scanned pages, no text layer: §V.A the table, §V.B the equal employee/employer split), which each CY advisory cites; /partners/employers/ContributionTable_v2.pdf is the superseded 2019-0009 infographic and is not an authority.
pagibigfund.gov.ph serves a reCAPTCHA page, not the PDF: cite Circular 460 (15 January 2024, from February 2024; the 1%/2% tiers and the ₱10,000 fund salary cap) from its copy annexed to DMW Advisory 37-2025 (https://wcms.dmw.gov.ph/uploads/DMW_ADVISORY_37_2025_01225b9fec.pdf, 6 scanned pages, Circular 460 on pp.2–6), and Circular 275 from the Wayback copy (https://web.archive.org/web/2020id_/https://www.pagibigfund.gov.ph/document/pdf/circulars/provident/HDMF%20Circular%20275%20-%20Implementing%20Guidelines%20on%20Employer%20Registration%20Contribution%20and%20Remittance.pdf).
bir.gov.ph — bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/local/pdf/Annex E RR 11-2018.pdf is the withholding table (monthly and semi-monthly columns, 0.3 MB); revenue regulation digests are under bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/.
nwpc.dole.gov.ph — regional wage orders: /ncr/, /region-iva/ (and the other regions); /bwc-handbook-workers-statutory-monetary-benefits/ is the DOLE Handbook (factors, premiums, 13th month).
pco.gov.ph answers 403 to the reader; use the Gazette.

Finding changes (read these before comparing, every run):
Wage orders: read https://nwpc.dole.gov.ph/feed/ (RSS) for new RTWPB orders, then open https://nwpc.dole.gov.ph/statistics/summary-of-latest-wage-orders-issued-by-the-regional-boards/ and follow its 'Download PDF' (Latest-Wage-Order-Matrix-<date>.pdf, a text PDF with issue/publication/effectivity per region). Effectivity is 15 days after publication when the matrix leaves it blank. The regional pages (/ncr/, /region-iva/ …) link the signed wage-order PDFs. These are scans with no text layer, so take the figures from the matrix. SSS: newest CI number on /sss-circulars/, and the rate table on /pay-contribution/. PhilHealth: /advisories/<YYYY>/ and /circulars/<YYYY>/; premium changes are 'Premium Contribution … for CY<YYYY>' advisories. BIR: every www.bir.gov.ph listing (RR, RMC, WithHoldingTax) is a client-rendered shell ('Loading…'), so it cannot be read. Discover RR/RMC numbers from a big-4 alert list (PwC PH Tax Alerts, SGV/EY Tax Bulletin), then open the PDF at https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/RR%20No.%20<n>-<yyyy>.pdf. Holidays: lawphil proclamation index for discovery only (officialgazette.gov.ph returns 403). Pag-IBIG and DOLE/BWC labor advisories are bot-walled: use news only to discover, and do not cite them.

facts.label: Regularly fewer than ten employees
facts.description: Whether the establishment regularly employs fewer than ten employees: outside service incentive leave (Labor Code art.95(b); Omnibus Rules Book III Rule V s.1(e); DOLE Handbook on Workers’ Statutory Monetary Benefits 2023, SIL B.8). A count of the establishment, with no statutory default: required.

facts.label: Retail, service or agricultural establishment of ten or fewer
facts.description: Whether the establishment is a retail, service or agricultural establishment or operation employing not more than ten employees: outside RA 7641 retirement pay (Labor Code art.302). A different test from `small_establishment` (any sector, fewer than ten), with no statutory default: required.

facts.label: Exempted from the wage order by the regional board
facts.description: Whether the regional wages board has approved this establishment's application for exemption from the wage order in force (RA 6727 s.4(c); DOLE Administrative Order No. 264, series of 2026, on exemptions). Without it a covered contract below the floor refuses the run. Default false: an exemption exists only once approved.

obligations.timing: Promptly on employment; the employer is relieved of liability for an unreported employee only for a contingency within 30 days of employment (RA 11199 s.24(a))

obligations.description: Transmit the employee's pregnancy notice to SSS, advance the full maternity benefit, claim reimbursement, and pay the salary differential unless exempt (distressed; retail/service of 10 or fewer; micro business of ₱3M assets or less; already paying equal or better)

obligations.description: Pay rank-and-file employees (kasambahay included) at least 1/12 of the basic salary earned in the calendar year, pro rata to a leaver, and report compliance to DOLE

obligations.description: Pay wages on a regular schedule: not less than once every two weeks or twice a month at intervals not exceeding 16 days; a kasambahay at least once a month; hotel and restaurant service charges distributed in full on the same cadence

obligations.authority: Labor Code art.103; Omnibus Rules Book III Rule VIII s.3 (https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/85819); RA 10361 s.25; Labor Code art.96 as amended by RA 11360 (Handbook ch.6 §D, https://nwpc.dole.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/Workers-Statutory-Monetary-Benefits-Handbook-2024-Edition.pdf)

obligations.description: Pay at least the regional wage order rate for the establishment's area and sector from the order's effective date (NCR-26 from 18 July 2025; NCR-28 from 26 September 2026; IVA-22 from 5 October 2025 with its 1 April 2026 tranche; kasambahay orders such as NCR-DW-06 from 7 February 2026)

exit_facts.label: Labor Code authorised cause
exit_facts.description: The authorised cause of an employer's termination (Labor Code arts. 298–299); the broad exit reason does not tell labour-saving devices from retrenchment, or a closure for serious losses from one without.

exit_facts.label: Terminated for disease (Labor Code art.299)
exit_facts.description: Whether the employer ended the employment because the employee suffers from a disease whose continued employment is prohibited by law or prejudicial to the employee's or co-employees' health (Labor Code art.299, formerly art.284; E-Library PD 442 text art.323). The employer must pay separation pay of at least one month's salary or half a month per year of service, whichever is greater, a fraction of at least six months counting as a year. Asked on every non-domestic dismissal or unilateral termination; a kasambahay's disease is a just cause without separation pay (RA 10361 s.34(f)). Added in place 2026-09-29 in every version (a transcription omission: the article predates every version).

exit_facts.label: Kasambahay dismissed without just cause
exit_facts.description: Whether a domestic worker was dismissed without a cause RA 10361 s.34 lists: an unjust dismissal pays the compensation earned plus fifteen days’ work as indemnity (s.32).

exit_facts.label: Kasambahay left without justifiable reason
exit_facts.description: RA 10361 s.32: unpaid salary of up to fifteen days is forfeited when the worker leaves without justifiable reason.

name: Philippines — 7 February 2026 — withholding correction R45 (R46 withholding registration)
void_reason: Superseded by 37a41753-0090-5187-b41a-473bbd8cedf6 to refuse SSS/MPF assessment when compulsory-coverage age is unknown; original catalogues retained.
change_summary: Wage Order No. NCR-DW-06 (approved 15 January 2026, published 22 January 2026 in The Philippine Star, effective 7 February 2026; nwpc.dole.gov.ph/ncr/): NCR domestic-worker (kasambahay) minimum wage ₱7,000 → ₱7,800 a month (`wages.by_employment_type.DOMESTIC.NCR`). Nothing else moves. Correction R45, 26 September 2026: RR 11-2018 s.2.79(B)(3),(5)(a). Taxable regular compensation excludes variable overtime/night premiums and leave encashment; deduct mandatory contributions before testing the cumulative trigger; ordinary withholding retains the regular-pay bracket. Corrects the snapshot without changing statutory commencement dates, tax rates or exemption ceilings. R46: missing registration does not waive compulsory SSS, mandatory provident fund, EC, PhilHealth or HDMF contributions, nor BIR RR 11-2018 s.9 withholding by the applicable table; each scheme still applies its coverage and rate rules.

limits.authority: Labor Code of the Philippines art.83

RA 10361 s.20: "an aggregate daily rest period of eight (8) hours per day", so at most sixteen worked hours in a day; a break is rest (https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/51514). The weekly rest (s.21, 24 consecutive hours a week) is met by `weekly_rest`, a rest after six consecutive work days (Labor Code art.91), which leaves no calendar week without one.

work_rules.authority: Labor Code of the Philippines (P.D. 442, as amended) Book III: art.82 (coverage), art.83 (eight-hour day), art.85 (meal period), art.86 (night shift differential), art.87 (overtime), art.91 (weekly rest day), art.93 (rest-day premium) and art.94 (holiday pay), with Proclamation No. 1006, s.2025 for the 2026 regular holidays and special (non-working) days. Applied 2026-09-18 (2): art.86 and Handbook ch.5: the night shift differential is 10% of the hour’s own rate, so 13 on a rest day or a special day, 20 on a regular holiday, 26 on a regular holiday falling on the rest day, 15 on a special day on the rest day, and on the overtime hours of each 12.5, 16.9, 26, 33.8 and 19.5 (`night_premium` adds as expressions over the day; the first eight night hours of a rest day or holiday are its ordinary ones). Handbook ch.2 §D–E: a monthly-paid employee — one "paid every day of the month, including unworked rest days, special days, and regular holidays", declared on the contract as `terms.paid_rest_days` (applied 2026-09-23, round 4: the payroll group is the employer’s own label and states no law) — is prorated and has an absence deducted on the 365 factor, 30.4167 a month (`proration_by`); the daily-paid keep 21.75 or 26.0833. Applied 2026-09-19 (2): The night-differential ladder reads the day type (`day_type`, which the holiday takes under `holiday_rest_precedence: PUBLIC_HOLIDAY`); `holiday.kind` is the published row’s kind (PUBLIC | SPECIAL | SUBSTITUTE), and a day-type literal against it never matched. Applied 2026-09-23 (PH audit): Handbook ch.2 §D, ch.3 §C, ch.4 §D state each day's pay as a total — a regular holiday worked 200%, a special day 130%, a rest day 130%, a regular holiday on the rest day 260%, a special day on the rest day 150%. The salary (261, 313 and 365 factors alike) and the daily-paid roster already pay a working holiday at 100%, so its first eight hours add the rest: 100% and 30% (`OT-2.0X`, `OT-1.3X`). The 365 factor (`terms.paid_rest_days`) also pays the rest day in the salary, so on it the rest-day rows add 30%, 160% and 50%; every other employee's rest day is unpaid and the rows carry the whole 130%, 260% and 150%. Hours beyond eight are paid by no base and keep their whole 169%, 260%, 338% and 195%. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 2): DOLE Handbook (2022) ch.2 §C: where two regular holidays fall on one day (a `DOUBLE_HOLIDAY` calendar row), the day is at least 200% of the daily wage unworked (`DOUBLE-HOLIDAY-UNWORKED`: a second day’s wage) and 300% worked (`OT-3.0X`: two more days on top of the day the wage pays); the guide computations (ch.4 §D) give 390% on a rest day (`OT-3.9X-REST`, 290% for the 365-factor employee, `terms.paid_rest_days`, whose salary pays the rest day), overtime 3 × 1.3 = 390% (`OT-3.9X`) and 3.9 × 1.3 = 507% on a rest day (`OT-5.07X-REST`), and night shift 10% of those rates (30, 39; overtime 39, 50.7). Ch.2 §D–E: an unworked regular holiday is paid only to an employee present, or on leave with pay, on the workday immediately preceding it (a rest or non-work day looks back further; two successive holidays pass the test through the first); `payroll.regular_holiday_prior_workday` applies it to the daily-paid wage and `holiday.prior_day_present` to the double holiday’s second day.

wages.authority: Applied 2026-09-18 (2): the wage orders state a daily rate; `by_region` carries it × 313/12 and `wages.scale` restates the floor on the person’s own factor — 365/12 for the monthly-paid, 261/12 on a five-day week, 313/12 on a six-day one — and the apprentice’s 75% (RA 6727; Labor Code arts.61, 75). Applied 2026-09-19 (3): Wage Order No. IVA-22 (effective 5 Oct 2025; nwpc.dole.gov.ph/region-iva): non-agriculture ₱600 in the Extended Metropolitan Area and the component cities (`IV-A`), ₱550 in 1st-class municipalities, ₱510 in reclassified 1st-class and 2nd–5th-class municipalities, the last two stepping to ₱550 and ₱525 on 1 April 2026 — the version from that date carries the second tranche. Each figure is the daily rate × 313 ÷ 12. Applied 2026-09-23 (audit): sector floors beside the area ones, for an establishment whose `company.region` names its sector — `NCR-AGRI-SMALL` is NCR agriculture, service/retail of 15 workers or fewer and manufacturing under 10 (₱658 under NCR-26, ₱718 under NCR-28; nwpc.dole.gov.ph/ncr/); `IV-A-RETAIL-SMALL` is IV-A retail/service of 10 workers or fewer (₱485 under IVA-22 from 5 Oct 2025, ₱508 from 1 Apr 2026; nwpc.dole.gov.ph/region-iva/). Each × 313 ÷ 12. The RA 9504 minimum-wage-earner test reads the same floor, so an employee of such an establishment above the sector floor is withheld on. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 2): RA 10361 (Batas Kasambahay) s.24: a domestic worker’s floor is the regional board’s domestic-worker wage order, a monthly figure, never the establishment order — `by_employment_type.DOMESTIC`, held on its own (scale 1). NCR only, from the wage orders themselves: NCR-DW-05 ₱7,000 a month from 4 January 2025, and NCR-DW-06 (approved 15 January 2026, published 22 January, effective 7 February 2026; nwpc.dole.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Wage-Order-No.-NCR-DW-06.pdf) ₱7,800 — this version states ₱7,800. Other regions’ domestic orders are not transcribed. Applied 2026-09-28 (issue 19, PH-A3): the floor is mandatory — RA 6727 s.4 and Wage Order No. NCR-28 s.4 (the increase applies to “all minimum wage earners in the private sector within the region”) and s.6 (non-payment is dealt with under RA 6727 s.12); only an exemption the board approves on application (RA 6727 s.4(c)) lowers it, recorded as `company.facts.minimum_wage_exemption_approved` (default false: no approval, no exemption). A covered under-floor contract therefore refuses the run (`block_below_when`). Applied 2026-09-30 (PH-A3 re-verification): a part-timer is refused too. The order’s daily rate is for normal working hours of at most eight a day and covers every minimum wage earner regardless of status (NCR-28 ss.3–4), and a worker on less than the normal hours is owed a proportion of it (DOLE Handbook 2024 ch.1 §L), so `wages.scale` multiplies a PART_TIME contract’s floor by its weekly hours over the full-time week of the person’s own factor (40 on a five-day week, 48 on a six-day one): the reference week is a recorded default, the orders naming none (20 hours on a five-day NCR-26 week: 695 × 261 ÷ 12 × 20 ÷ 40 = 7,558.13). The message quotes the floor on the person's own factor (₱755 × 261 ÷ 12 = 16,421.25 on a five-day week), not the 313-day basis. Applied 2026-09-29 (signed NWPC board orders): additional private daily rates are II ₱500, CAR ₱505, IV-B ₱455; domestic monthly rates are I ₱6,700, II ₱6,500, III ₱6,500, IV-A ₱6,750, V ₱6,000, VI ₱6,500, XII ₱6,000, VII ₱7,000, CAR ₱6,600, IV-B ₱7,000, XIII ₱6,500, X ₱6,500, BARMM ₱5,500. The order PDFs are in this version’s sources. The private-sector exemption approval fact cannot displace a domestic floor; the inspected orders that address exemption expressly disallow it. Unrepresented mid-interval cutovers, area/sector/headcount selection and worksite-region selection remain open. Signed uniform private-sector tranche rates added for complete sealed intervals only: V ₱435/day, XIII ₱455/day. Region V RBV-22 reaches ₱435 on 1 December 2025; Caraga RXIII-19 reaches ₱435 on 1 May 2025 and RXIII-20 sets ₱455 from 3 January 2026, ₱475 from 1 May 2026. Intervals containing a later tranche remain without that regional rate pending an exact sealed version boundary.

encashment.day_amount: terms.pay_frequency == "WEEKLY" ? terms.basic_salary / (terms.paid_rest_days ? 7.0 : terms.working_days_per_week) : terms.pay_frequency == "DAILY" ? terms.basic_salary : terms.pay_frequency == "HOURLY" ? terms.basic_salary * terms.ordinary_hours_per_week / terms.working_days_per_week : terms.basic_salary / (terms.paid_rest_days ? 365.0 / 12.0 : (terms.working_days_per_week >= 6.0 ? 313.0 : 261.0) / 12.0)
encashment.authority: DOLE Handbook on Workers Statutory Monetary Benefits, Service Incentive Leave, Conversion: salary rate on the conversion date, with pro-rata conversion. A daily contract supplies its daily salary; an hourly contract uses its normal scheduled hours per workday. Monthly equivalent factors follow paid-day coverage. Standing allowances require express basic-salary classification. https://nwpc.dole.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/Workers-Statutory-Monetary-Benefits-Handbook-2024-Edition.pdf Applied 2026-09-23 (round 5): a weekly contract converts at the same salary rate on the conversion date — its week's wage over the days that wage pays: the working days of the week, or all seven where the contract pays the rest day too (the Handbook's monthly-paid/daily-paid distinction, Rules on EEMR factors 365 and 313/261, applied to a week).

benefit_cases.authority: RA 11210 ss.3 and 5 and its IRR: 105 days' maternity leave with full pay for a live birth, 60 for a miscarriage or emergency termination, 15 more for a qualified solo parent, at least 60 days after delivery; the SSS maternity benefit is the average daily salary credit (the six highest of the twelve monthly salary credits, capped at PHP 20,000, before the semester of contingency, divided by 180) times the compensable days, with at least three monthly contributions paid in that twelve-month window, for a contingency on or after 11 March 2019; the employer advances it within 30 days of the application and SSS reimburses it. DOLE Department Advisory 01-2019 ss.II–IV: the salary differential is full pay (monthly salary × days ÷ 30) less the employee's SSS, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG shares and the SSS benefit, never negative; the exemption categories need DOLE approval. BIR RMC 105-2019: both are exempt from withholding. RA 11861 ss.15 and 20: the solo-parent identification card or eligibility certificate, first-time applicants within six months of the event.

sources.instructions:
Sources are the primary instrument first — the statute or regulation in the national law database, the gazette, or the table the authority itself publishes — one page per fact the version seals, never a news article or a commentary. A historical version lists the instruments in force on its own effective date. Where the primary host refuses the reader (sso.agc.gov.sg, officialgazette.gov.ph, peraturan.bpk.go.id, kwsp.gov.my, hrdcorp.gov.my answer 403 to Norbital-Public-Page-Reader) the authority’s own published table is listed instead, or the Wayback Machine’s dated copy of the authority’s own page or PDF (web.archive.org/web/<timestamp>id_/<url>) — never a host the reader cannot open.
officialgazette.gov.ph — the Official Gazette: Republic Acts, proclamations, executive orders. A proclamation is /<yyyy>/<mm>/<dd>/proclamation-no-<n>-s-<year>/ (HTML, full text); /section/proclamations/ lists the newest first; /nationwide-holidays/<year>/ is the holiday calendar. lawphil.net mirrors the same texts and is corroboration only.
sss.gov.ph — /pay-contribution/ carries the contribution schedule (the 2025 table PDF under /wp-content/uploads/ is 6.3 MB, over the reader limit: read the HTML page); /sss-circulars/ lists circulars by year.
philhealth.gov.ph — /advisories/<year>/ lists advisories; each is /advisories/<year>/PA<year>-<nnnn>.pdf (small, text). the premium schedule is PhilHealth Circular 2020-0005 (Revision 1), /circulars/2020/circ2020-0005.pdf (5 scanned pages, no text layer: §V.A the table, §V.B the equal employee/employer split), which each CY advisory cites; /partners/employers/ContributionTable_v2.pdf is the superseded 2019-0009 infographic and is not an authority.
pagibigfund.gov.ph serves a reCAPTCHA page, not the PDF: cite Circular 460 (15 January 2024, from February 2024; the 1%/2% tiers and the ₱10,000 fund salary cap) from its copy annexed to DMW Advisory 37-2025 (https://wcms.dmw.gov.ph/uploads/DMW_ADVISORY_37_2025_01225b9fec.pdf, 6 scanned pages, Circular 460 on pp.2–6), and Circular 275 from the Wayback copy (https://web.archive.org/web/2020id_/https://www.pagibigfund.gov.ph/document/pdf/circulars/provident/HDMF%20Circular%20275%20-%20Implementing%20Guidelines%20on%20Employer%20Registration%20Contribution%20and%20Remittance.pdf).
bir.gov.ph — bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/local/pdf/Annex E RR 11-2018.pdf is the withholding table (monthly and semi-monthly columns, 0.3 MB); revenue regulation digests are under bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/.
nwpc.dole.gov.ph — regional wage orders: /ncr/, /region-iva/ (and the other regions); /bwc-handbook-workers-statutory-monetary-benefits/ is the DOLE Handbook (factors, premiums, 13th month).
pco.gov.ph answers 403 to the reader; use the Gazette.

Finding changes (read these before comparing, every run):
Wage orders: read https://nwpc.dole.gov.ph/feed/ (RSS) for new RTWPB orders, then open https://nwpc.dole.gov.ph/statistics/summary-of-latest-wage-orders-issued-by-the-regional-boards/ and follow its 'Download PDF' (Latest-Wage-Order-Matrix-<date>.pdf, a text PDF with issue/publication/effectivity per region). Effectivity is 15 days after publication when the matrix leaves it blank. The regional pages (/ncr/, /region-iva/ …) link the signed wage-order PDFs. These are scans with no text layer, so take the figures from the matrix. SSS: newest CI number on /sss-circulars/, and the rate table on /pay-contribution/. PhilHealth: /advisories/<YYYY>/ and /circulars/<YYYY>/; premium changes are 'Premium Contribution … for CY<YYYY>' advisories. BIR: every www.bir.gov.ph listing (RR, RMC, WithHoldingTax) is a client-rendered shell ('Loading…'), so it cannot be read. Discover RR/RMC numbers from a big-4 alert list (PwC PH Tax Alerts, SGV/EY Tax Bulletin), then open the PDF at https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/RR%20No.%20<n>-<yyyy>.pdf. Holidays: lawphil proclamation index for discovery only (officialgazette.gov.ph returns 403). Pag-IBIG and DOLE/BWC labor advisories are bot-walled: use news only to discover, and do not cite them.

facts.label: Regularly fewer than ten employees
facts.description: Whether the establishment regularly employs fewer than ten employees: outside service incentive leave (Labor Code art.95(b); Omnibus Rules Book III Rule V s.1(e); DOLE Handbook on Workers’ Statutory Monetary Benefits 2023, SIL B.8). A count of the establishment, with no statutory default: required.

facts.label: Retail, service or agricultural establishment of ten or fewer
facts.description: Whether the establishment is a retail, service or agricultural establishment or operation employing not more than ten employees: outside RA 7641 retirement pay (Labor Code art.302). A different test from `small_establishment` (any sector, fewer than ten), with no statutory default: required.

facts.label: Exempted from the wage order by the regional board
facts.description: Whether the regional wages board has approved this establishment's application for exemption from the wage order in force (RA 6727 s.4(c); DOLE Administrative Order No. 264, series of 2026, on exemptions). Without it a covered contract below the floor refuses the run. Default false: an exemption exists only once approved.

obligations.description: Transmit the employee's pregnancy notice to SSS, advance the full maternity benefit, claim reimbursement, and pay the salary differential unless exempt (distressed; retail/service of 10 or fewer; micro business of ₱3M assets or less; already paying equal or better)

obligations.owner: HR / SSS maternity notification and reimbursement claim; Finance / differential

obligations.description: Remit the month's PhilHealth premium (both shares) through the Electronic Premium Remittance System with its remittance report

exit_facts.label: Labor Code authorised cause
exit_facts.description: The authorised cause of an employer's termination (Labor Code arts. 298–299); the broad exit reason does not tell labour-saving devices from retrenchment, or a closure for serious losses from one without.

exit_facts.label: Terminated for disease (Labor Code art.299)
exit_facts.description: Whether the employer ended the employment because the employee suffers from a disease whose continued employment is prohibited by law or prejudicial to the employee's or co-employees' health (Labor Code art.299, formerly art.284; E-Library PD 442 text art.323). The employer must pay separation pay of at least one month's salary or half a month per year of service, whichever is greater, a fraction of at least six months counting as a year. Asked on every non-domestic dismissal or unilateral termination; a kasambahay's disease is a just cause without separation pay (RA 10361 s.34(f)). Added in place 2026-09-29 in every version (a transcription omission: the article predates every version).

exit_facts.label: Kasambahay dismissed without just cause
exit_facts.description: Whether a domestic worker was dismissed without a cause RA 10361 s.34 lists: an unjust dismissal pays the compensation earned plus fifteen days’ work as indemnity (s.32).

exit_facts.label: Kasambahay left without justifiable reason
exit_facts.description: RA 10361 s.32: unpaid salary of up to fifteen days is forfeited when the worker leaves without justifiable reason.
